headline: Off-site road improvement agreement with Procopio approved, allowing 25 certificates of occupancy before the Pillsbury Road left-turn lane is finished.
summary: The left-turn lane on Pillsbury Road must be substantially complete by November 15th, 2027, and Procopio will add a stop sign and crosswalks at Michael's Way. The agreement still needs Planning Board approval, set for December 2nd. A tentative contract with IAFF Local 3160, the firefighters union, was also approved, pending voter approval of its cost items. A public hearing on the proposed water special assessment district was set for November 30th.
decisions: Approved the off-site improvements agreement with Procopio, 4-1, letting the acting town manager enter into it.
Approved the tentative contract with IAFF Local 3160 for 2027 through 2030, subject to voter approval of cost items.
Scheduled a public hearing for November 30th, 2026 on the proposed water special assessment district, 5-0.
discussion: Procopio occupancy and bond: Members questioned whether 25 certificates of occupancy could be issued before the left-turn lane is finished and what protects the town if the project stalls. Staff said the road network can handle 25 occupancies and that a site restoration bond would cover a stalled site.

Legal services budget: The proposed FY 28 legal services line is $420,000, up from $200,000 this year and in the default budget, and the main firm's hourly rate rose to $375 in July. Staff said six union contracts are expected to start in January, and that their legal costs add up fast.

Assistant town manager: The proposed town manager budget is $547,062, which is $160,269 less than fiscal year 27 because the cost of an assistant position was removed. Staff said succession planning matters and suggested a stipend, while members questioned why past assistant positions were not used when the job was vacant.

Community Health Services contract: The town pays $81,000 to Community Health Services, which handles general assistance intake. Members questioned whether it gives good value and asked for information on other providers, and staff said they would bring that information back.

Fire chief pay raise: A resident said the fire chief received a $15,000 pay scale increase and a later raise of about $9,000, including $5,075.20 paid as a lump sum above the maximum. The resident asked the town to look into the payments and said the library makes similar payments.

decision_evidence.quote: I move that the Londonderry Town Council hereby authorize the acting town manager to enter into the off-site improvements agreement and to take all actions necessary to effectuate the agreement. ... Chair votes in the affirmative. 4-1.

I move that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approve the tentative successor uh collective bargaining agreement between the town and IAFF Local 3160 for July 20- July 1st, 2027 through June 30th, 2030, subject to the voter approval of applicable cost items and other required approvals. ... Any opposed? Shows to be unanimous.

I move that the Londonderry Town Council hereby schedules a public hearing on November 30th, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. in the Moose Hill council chambers at the Londonderry Town Hall on the proposed water special assessment district. ... Any opposed? Shows affirmative. Thank you very much. 5-0.
